question: to the Commission Jean-Paul Garraud (PfE), Christophe Bay (PfE) Subject:

Since 1 May 2026, the Interim Trade Agreement between the European Union and the Mercosur countries has been provisionally applied with Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay1. The Commission is presenting this agreement as an opportunity for EU exports, including industrial and agri-food exports. However, it also exposes the EU market to sensitive quotas, including 99 000 tonnes of beef at a reduced tariff rate, 180 000 tonnes of poultry, 450 000 tonnes of ethanol for the chemical industry and other agricultural products. For years, French and European farmers have warned of the risk of unfair competition, particularly when imports do not comply with health, environmental and social standards equivalent to those in force in the EU. In view of the above: Will the Commission publish a monitoring report showing import volumes, prices and the impact on agricultural profits, broken down by industry?
https://trade.ec.europa.eu/access-to-markets/en/news/application-eu-mercosur-interim-trade-agreement-1may-2026
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (29.6.2026) According to Article 4 of Regulation (EU) 2026/687 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 11 March 2026 implementing the bilateral safeguard clauses of the EU-Mercosur Partnership Agreement and the EU-Mercosur Interim Trade Agreement for agricultural products1, the Commission shall constantly and proactively monitor the EU market of sensitive products listed in Annex I to the Regulation in particular as regards import and export trends, production and price developments, with the support of the EU market observatories established under Regulation (EU) No 1308/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council2. For this purpose, the Commission shall cooperate and exchange data with Member States, the European Parliament and the EU industry on a regular basis. In line with Regulation (EU) 2026/687, the Commission will present a monitoring report to the European Parliament and to the Council at least every six months containing its assessment of the impact of imports of sensitive products benefitting from preferential market access under the Agreement. The first one is scheduled to be presented before the end of 2026.
1 OJ L, 2026/687, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2026/687/oj. 2 OJ L 347, 20.12.2013, pp. 671–854, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2013/1308/oj.
